result.title: A Definition of Catastrophic Performance
result.summary: A central challenge in AI is specifying objectives that align with human preferences. While existing theoretical results elucidate how misspecification impacts performance, they typically do not distinguish between merely suboptimal and catastrophic outcomes. To enable rigorous analysis of catastrophic risk from AI misalignment, we introduce a formal definition of catastrophic performance. Our definition is based on two reference values. The first, baseline value, captures the value attained if no agent is deployed. The second, orthogonal value, captures the value of a trajectory that is unrelated to human preferences, in a sense we describe. Orthogonal value is typically far worse than baseline value. We interpret these reference values through examples in which past human activity has altered the state of the environment to human benefit. Starting at the resulting state, an AI agent is deployed with the goal of accelerating further progress. Catastrophic performance represents this agent's undoing of benefits afforded by human activity.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出「灾难性表现」的形式化定义，用「基线价值」与「正交价值」两个参照值刻画 AI 代理撤销人类既有收益的情形，属于对齐目标设定的理论研究。
AI.relevance_reason: 全文围绕价值目标与灾难性风险的定义，未涉及视觉细节表示、latent 推理状态生成、证据使用或停止决策，也没有可供迁移的具体方法线索，故排除。
